text: The convergence analysis considers a convex-Lipschitz loss function $f$ with gradient norm bounded by $\rho$, i.e., $\|\boldsymbol{v}_t\|\le \rho$ for per-iteration gradient vectors $\boldsymbol{v}_t$, and an update rule $\boldsymbol{w}^{(t+1)}=\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\eta\boldsymbol{v}_t$ applied sequentially over $T$ steps; with $\boldsymbol{w}^*$ any comparator vector, for any $B_m< B_p < B$, where $B_m=\|\boldsymbol{w}_m^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$ with $\boldsymbol{w}_m$ denoting the effective weighted parameters when masks $\boldsymbol{m}$ are applied, $B_p=\|\boldsymbol{w}_p^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$ with $\boldsymbol{w}_p$ denoting the prompt-only effective parameters (with $\boldsymbol{m}=\mathbf{1}$), and $\|\boldsymbol{w}^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\| \le B$, choosing $\eta=\sqrt{B^2/(\rho^2 T)}$ yields the bound $$ \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\langle \boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*,\boldsymbol{v}_t\rangle \le \frac{B_m\rho}{\sqrt{T}} < \frac{B_p\rho}{\sqrt{T}} < \frac{B\rho}{\sqrt{T}}. $$

label: assertion
text: The convergence analysis considers a convex-Lipschitz loss function $f$ with gradient norm bounded by $\rho$, i.e., $\|\boldsymbol{v}_t\|\le \rho$ for per-iteration gradient vectors $\boldsymbol{v}_t$, and an update rule $\boldsymbol{w}^{(t+1)}=\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\eta\boldsymbol{v}_t$ applied sequentially over $T$ steps; with $\overline{\boldsymbol{w}}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}$, $\boldsymbol{w}^*$ any comparator vector, and $B_m=\|\boldsymbol{w}_m^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$ where $\boldsymbol{w}_m$ denotes the effective weighted parameters when masks $\boldsymbol{m}$ are applied, the sub-optimality $f(\overline{\boldsymbol{w}})-f(\boldsymbol{w}^*)$ is upper-bounded by quantities that scale as $\mathcal{O}(B_m\rho/\sqrt{T})$.

label: assertion
text: With $B_m=\|\boldsymbol{w}_m^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$, where $\boldsymbol{w}_m$ denotes the effective weighted parameters when masks $\boldsymbol{m}$ are applied, and with $\boldsymbol{w}_p$ denoting the prompt-only effective parameters (with $\boldsymbol{m}=\mathbf{1}$), a smaller $B_m$ (associated with learning soft masks) yields a tighter bound than prompt-only or unconstrained updates.
